name: Layer42

profile.address: 3080, Raymond Street, Santa Clara, Santa Clara County, California, 95054
profile.reading:
The building at 3080 Raymond Street in Santa Clara, California carries the name Layer42 in this record, but the company that name refers to has not operated the building under its own brand for close to a decade. Layer42 Networks was founded in 1999 as a Silicon Valley business-to-business connectivity and colocation provider, eventually running about 70,000 square feet of data center space across sites in Santa Clara and Mountain View and serving roughly 150 customers, including well-known names like Dropbox, Square, and Barracuda Networks. On September 11, 2015, regional broadband and business-services provider Wave Broadband acquired Layer42 Networks outright and rebranded the unit "Layer42 by Wave," keeping Layer42's former CEO on as a senior data-center-services executive.

The Raymond Street building itself is documented in trade press coverage of a later transaction: at roughly 30,000 square feet with about 3 megawatts of total facility capacity, of which roughly 1.5 megawatts was available for colocation customers, it was one of the facilities Wave Broadband owned when Wave sold its Santa Clara data center business to VPLS in November 2021. VPLS rebranded the site "SV3" after the purchase. In other words, the chain of ownership runs from Layer42 Networks (pre-2015, independent), to Wave Broadband / "Layer42 by Wave" (2015-2021), to VPLS / SV3 (2021 onward) -- meaning the "Layer42" name attached to this address is a legacy brand from an ownership period that ended years ago rather than a description of who runs the building today.

For a small-to-midsize Silicon Valley colocation facility of this vintage and size, 3 megawatts of total capacity and 30,000 square feet puts it well below the scale of the hyperscale and wholesale campuses that have since come to dominate Santa Clara's data center market, more in line with a carrier-neutral facility built to serve network, cloud, and enterprise colocation customers needing proximity to Silicon Valley peering points rather than large single-tenant deployments. No additional detail on cooling architecture, redundancy tier, or current occupancy under VPLS/SV3 ownership was found in public reporting. Readers researching this address for current operational status should treat "Layer42" as a historical name rather than the facility's present operator.

reading:
Layer42 Networks was a Silicon Valley metro Ethernet and business internet provider, not a data centre landlord in the way the colocation label suggests, and it no longer exists as an independent company. It ran autonomous system 8121 and sold internet access, Ethernet transport and wavelength services from 10 Mbps to 100 Gbps across the South Bay, San Francisco and the Mountain View corridor. At the point it was sold it had roughly 150 customers, among them Barracuda Networks, Dropbox and Square, and it operated two network operations centres, one in Santa Clara and one in Mountain View, offering about 70,000 square feet of colocation between them.

Wave Broadband bought Layer42 in September 2015 on undisclosed terms and ran it as Layer42 by Wave, with founder and chief executive Derek Garnier joining Wave as senior vice president of data centre services. Wave later left the colocation business in Santa Clara. On 22 November 2021 VPLS acquired the former Layer42 and Wave building, describing 30,000 square feet of usable space, 3 MW of total facility capacity of which 1.5 MW was available to colocation customers, and access to more than twenty native fibre providers. VPLS has since rebranded as Evocative, and the building recorded here under Layer42, at 3080 Raymond Street in Santa Clara, is now Evocative's SJC3. The peering database entry for AS8121 tells the same story. It is titled Wave Datacenters, formerly known as Layer42, and carries a note that the network is being merged into AS11404, with its remaining presence listed at facilities owned by CoreSite, Equinix, Digital Realty, QTS and Evocative rather than at anything Layer42 owns.

The Raymond Street block also gives a clean illustration of how power figures get mixed up. In June 2023 the City of Santa Clara adopted an environmental determination for the adjoining property at 3060 Raymond Street, a 1.7 acre site, covering seismic upgrades and an increase in the power supply from 1.6 MW to 9 MW delivered as two 4.5 MW feeds, together with five 2,000 kilowatt diesel standby generators and five 427 ton free cooling chillers. The 9 MW is utility service, the 10 MW of diesel is standby generation that runs only when the utility fails, and neither is the same as saleable IT load. Directories tend to print whichever of the three is largest.

Nothing in this research established a current headquarters, founding year or ownership for Layer42 as a standalone entity, because there is not one to establish. The row should be read as a historical operator record whose building has since changed hands twice, and the single California facility attached to it should be reconciled to Evocative rather than counted as a Layer42 site.
